commit_message:
[Merged] [truetype] Fix Savannah bug #35601.

* src/truetype/ttinterp.c (Ins_SHZ): Use number of points instead of
last point for loop.
Also remove redundant boundary check.
pr_title: [truetype] Fix SHZ range limit to use validated point count
pr_description:
The `Ins_SHZ` handler previously computed the number of points to shift in the normal zone by reading `contours[n_contours - 1] + 1` — a font-supplied value that could exceed the actual number of allocated points.

This change computes the limit directly from `n_points - 4` (subtracting the four phantom points that TrueType appends), which is always bounded by the validated point count and never derived from font-controlled contour data.

The comment is updated accordingly: the normal zone's `n_points` includes phantom points, so we subtract them rather than relying on the contours array to find the end of real points.

fix_commit_message:
* src/truetype/ttinterp.c (Ins_SHZ): Fix the range limit.

Fixes #1419 and #1420, as well as
    https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/499455833
agent_reasoning: The buggy code derived `limit` for the SHZ shift loop from `contours[n_contours-1] + 1`, a font-controlled value with no bounds check against the actual number of allocated points. A malformed font could supply a contour end-index larger than `n_points`, causing the loop to read/write beyond the heap-allocated points arrays (buffer overflow). The fixed code computes `limit = n_points - 4U` for the normal zone, which is always within the validated allocation (TrueType zones always have exactly 4 phantom points appended), entirely eliminating the font-controlled out-of-bounds path.
